lesson_title: Squares, Cubes and Roots of Decimals
clip_script:
Picture a square mat with sides zero comma three metres — thirty centimetres, the size of a floor tile. Its area is side times side: zero comma three times zero comma three. Think in centimetres: thirty times thirty is nine hundred square centimetres. A square metre is one hundred by one hundred, ten thousand square centimetres. Nine hundred out of ten thousand is nine hundredths: zero comma zero nine square metres. Zero comma three squared is zero comma zero nine, and you can see why — the tile covers nine percent of a square metre, not ninety.

That is the sense check for every decimal square under one: the area number is smaller than the side number, because a side shorter than a metre covers less than a one-metre strip.

pacing: slow on the tile, quick on the rule
